Anna — thanks, this is exactly the kind of pattern that motivates a different commercial approach. Quick answers up front:

- Minimum billing increment for burst: standard is per-minute (rounded up), with a 10-minute cooldown by default.
- We can offer a burst-credit pool that amortizes minute-level spikes against monthly credits (see proposal below).
- Cooldown exceptions: we can provide a shortened cooldown on a per-account basis when paired with a committed baseline and monitoring-based burst gating.

I'm attaching a short pricing table and a draft SOW. Proposed commercial trade: if Nimbus commits to a 12-month baseline (5-node GPU pool) with a 20% reserved-commit discount, Redwood will:
  1) Provide a 3000-minute/month burst-credit pool (applies to sub-10-minute spikes)
  2) Reduce the default cooldown to 3 minutes for spikes covered by the credit pool
  3) Cap effective surge rate at 1.6x baseline GPU-hour for the first 12 months for any usage within the pool

This keeps short spikes from causing repeated minute-by-minute billing while preserving fairness for sustained overage. If spikes exceed the pool we fall back to the standard cooldown and surge rate.

If that sounds directionally OK I can run final numbers with finance and send a revised SOW.

Looping in pricing ops. Quick clarifications for Anna:

1) Concurrency and pool burn: credits are consumed per-minute per-GPU-equivalent. Overlapping spikes will consume more credits (the pool is capacity-based). We can model Ryzen-equivalent GPU units to match Nimbus's telemetry during the final SOW.

2) Visibility & alerts: Redwood Console will show minute-level burn with alerting thresholds. We'll include a standard alerting playbook.

3) Throughput guarantees: for the baseline 5-node pool we can commit to a sustained throughput target (tokens/sec) with a p95 latency SLO on typical request sizes; burst nodes are best-effort with a throughput uplift target but no hard p95 SLO unless you opt into a higher-tier SLA.

4) Grace buffer: we can offer a one-time 24-hour goodwill buffer for the first 6 months; after that anomaly protections rely on alerts + on-call escalation.

Pricing ops suggests a compromise on commit length: 9 months acceptable for a 10% additional baseline discount (on top of standard reserved rate) if Nimbus signs within 14 days of the revised SOW.

-M

Anna / procurement —

Thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Per your asks we've updated the commercial terms. Summary of the final proposal we will put in the revised SOW: 

1) Commit: 9-month baseline (5 GPU nodes) with the following pricing: baseline rate = reserved rate less 30% standard reserved discount less additional 10% commit incentive (final rate shown in attached pricing_table_v3.xlsx).
2) Burst-credit pool: 3000 GPU-minute credits / month. Credits are consumed per GPU-equivalent per-minute. Overlapping spikes consume multiple credits.
3) Cooldown / billing increments: default billing increment remains per-minute; when credits are available the effective cooldown for short spikes is 3 minutes (i.e., spikes < = 3 mins inside pool will not trigger min-10 billing).
4) Visibility & audit: Redwood Console will surface minute-level consumption and exportable audit logs for compliance. SOW will define "GPU-equivalent" mapping used for credit conversion.
5) Grace & remediation: one-time 24-hour provider-side-exposure grace; Redwood will replenish 10% of the monthly pool if provider-side outage is confirmed.
6) Surge rate cap: effective surge multiplier capped at 1.6x baseline for pool-covered minutes for 12 months. Excess usage billed at standard surge rates.

Next steps: if procurement confirms this language we will: (a) update SOW and Schedules, (b) run a short smoke test against your telemetry feed to validate GPU-equivalent mapping, and (c) prepare legal-ready attachments.

I've attached the pricing table and a draft SOW with tracked changes. If you want the CTO on a call we can schedule a 30-minute slot tomorrow.
